mainTopic: The man who leads the שעיר המשתלח, רבי אליעזר's unanswered questions, the deaths after the עגל, and the escort to the cliff.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא that learns from the words עִתִּי and אִישׁ about the man who leads the שעיר המשתלח. The ברייתא says he is chosen ahead of time, the goat is sent even on שבת and even in טומאה, and a זר may lead it. רב ששת explains that 'even on שבת' allows carrying a sick goat, and that this works even according to רבי נתן. רפרם learns from this that עירוב and הוצאה apply to שבת but not to יום הכיפורים. 'Even in טומאה' means an impure sender may enter the עזרה. Students then ask רבי אליעזר a series of questions, and he sidesteps each one, because he never said anything he had not heard from his teacher. A wise woman's question about why the sinners of the עגל died different deaths is answered by רב and לוי, and רב יהודה teaches that שבט לוי did not serve the עגל. The amud ends by explaining who the rude 'Babylonians' of the משנה were, and by starting a new משנה about the escort and the ten booths on the way to the cliff.

steps.title: The ברייתא's lessons from the word עִתִּי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from עִתִּי that the man must be prepared in advance, and that the goat is sent away even on שבת and even if the man is in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The word 'appointed' teaches] that he should be prepared ahead of time. 'Appointed' teaches: even on שבת. 'Appointed' teaches: even in a state of טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing the ברייתא's list of lessons from the word עִתִּי ('appointed') in the פסוק about sending away the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads עִתִּי in two ways. It can mean 'a man made ready ahead of time', so he is chosen the day before. It can also mean 'at its set time', so the sending happens no matter what, even on שבת and even when the man is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Appointed / timely'. The word in the פסוק describing the man who leads the goat away.
Prepared or designated ahead of time.
Ritual impurity.
The goat sent away to the wilderness on יום כיפור.

steps.confusionAlert: The first words of this amud, 'שֶׁיְּהֵא מְזוּמָּן', finish a sentence from the previous amud. The word עִתִּי that they explain appears there, just before this amud begins.

phrases.english: that he should be designated in advance.
phrases.notes: Explains עִתִּי, which was quoted on the previous amud.

phrases.english: 'Appointed' teaches: and even on Shabbat,
'Appointed' teaches: and even in a state of impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man is designated in advance, and the goat is sent away even on שבת and even when the man is in טומאה.

steps.title: Why do we need a פסוק to allow a זר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's lesson that אִישׁ allows a זר to lead the goat, and asks why this isn't obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A man' comes to allow a non-כהן. But isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to one line of the ברייתא, that the word אִישׁ allows a זר to lead the goat. It challenges this: why would a פסוק be needed for something so obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leading a goat into the wilderness is not a קרבן service done in the בית המקדש. So it seems clear that anyone may do it. If so, the ברייתא's teaching from אִישׁ looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A man'. The word in the פסוק for the one who leads the goat.
To make fit, or to allow.
A non-כהן (an ordinary Jew).
'It is obvious!' A challenge that a teaching is not needed.

phrases.english: 'A man' comes to qualify a non-priest.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes this line of the ברייתא in order to discuss it.

phrases.english: Isn't that obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to one of the ברייתא's lessons and questions whether it is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's teaching that אִישׁ allows a זר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sending away the goat is not a service on the מזבח, so of course a זר may do it. A פסוק should not be needed.

steps.title: The word כפרה could have misled us
steps.stepSummary: Without the word אִישׁ, we might have thought that only a כהן may lead the goat, because the תורה uses the word כפרה about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since 'atonement' is written about it, only a כהן may do it. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains what we would have mistakenly thought without the word אִישׁ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the goat brings כפרה, and כפרה is usually done through a כהן's service. So we might have required a כהן here too. The word אִישׁ tells us this כפרה is different, and even a זר may lead the goat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have said'. Introduces a mistaken assumption that the teaching comes to correct.
Atonement.
'It teaches us'. The teaching is needed to prevent that mistake.

phrases.english: You might have said:
'atonement' is written regarding it,
phrases.notes: So we would have assumed that only a כהן may do it.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows that a reasonable mistake was possible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the word כפרה is used, only a כהן may lead the goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a זר may lead the goat, despite the word כפרה.
steps.whatToRemember: The goat's role in כפרה might have suggested that a כהן is required, but the word אִישׁ allows a זר.

steps.title: What does 'even on שבת' actually permit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which שבת prohibition is being overridden by the lesson 'even on שבת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Appointed' teaches: even on שבת. For what practical law is this needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to another line of the ברייתא and asks what it is actually allowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking the goat to the wilderness does not seem to involve any מלאכה forbidden by the תורה. Going past the תחום is only a rabbinic prohibition. So the גמרא wants to know which real problem the פסוק is overriding.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For what law?' A request to find the practical difference a statement makes.
The day of rest. Here the question is about doing this service on it.

phrases.english: 'Appointed' teaches: and even on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again in order to analyze this line.

phrases.english: For what law is this needed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a different lesson of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which שבת prohibition is overridden by 'even on שבת'?

steps.title: רב ששת: he may carry a sick goat
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the teaching allows the man to carry the goat on his shoulder if it is sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: it is teaching that if the goat was sick, he carries it on his shoulder.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question and names the real שבת issue: carrying the goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goat cannot walk, the man has to carry it, and carrying can be a מלאכה forbidden by the תורה. The word עִתִּי shows that the sending must happen on time. That is why even this carrying is allowed on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer here.
Sick.
He sets it on his shoulder (carries it).

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: it comes to state
that if it (the goat) was sick,
he carries it on his shoulder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The teaching allows carrying a sick goat on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a general phrase ('even on שבת') into a specific case where a real prohibition of carrying is overridden.

steps.title: Does this go against רבי נתן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב ששת does not follow רבי נתן, who holds that a living creature 'carries itself'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? Not רבי נתן's. For if it were רבי נתן's, doesn't he say that a living being carries itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא רב ששת's answer fits, and suggests it cannot fit רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן holds חי נושא את עצמו: a living creature helps carry itself, so carrying it is not a תורה-level מלאכה. According to him, carrying the goat would not need a special allowance. So רב ששת's answer seems not to fit רבי נתן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to whom?' Asks which opinion a statement follows.
A תנא with an opinion about carrying living beings on שבת.
'A living being carries itself'. Carrying it is not a תורה-level מלאכה.

phrases.english: According to whom? Not according to Rabbi Natan.
For if it were Rabbi Natan, doesn't he say:
a living being carries itself?
phrases.notes: So according to him, carrying the goat would not be a תורה prohibition at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב ששת's answer against the views of the תנאים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's explanation of 'even on שבת'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי נתן, carrying a living creature is not a תורה prohibition, so the פסוק would not need to allow it.

steps.title: A sick animal is different
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי נתן agrees that a sick creature does not 'carry itself', so רב ששת's answer works for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this follows רבי נתן: a sick animal is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the claim that רב ששת disagrees with רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן's rule depends on the creature helping to carry itself. A sick goat cannot help at all, so it is like dead weight. Carrying it is therefore a real מלאכה even according to רבי נתן, and the פסוק is needed to allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You can even say'. Shows that a statement fits even the opinion that seemed to contradict it.
'A sick one is different'.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Natan:
a sick one is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רב ששת goes against רבי נתן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי נתן's rule only covers a healthy creature that can help carry itself, not a sick one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Carrying a sick goat is a real מלאכה according to everyone, and the word עִתִּי allows it on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: חי נושא את עצמו applies only to a creature that can help carry itself. A sick animal is dead weight, so carrying it is a real מלאכה.

steps.title: רפרם's inference: carrying rules apply to שבת but not יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רפרם infers from the 'even on שבת' teaching that עירוב and הוצאה apply to שבת and not to יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם said: This teaches us that עירוב and the ban on carrying out apply to שבת. They do not apply to יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם draws a conclusion from what we just learned: the תורה needed a special teaching to allow carrying the goat on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We said that עִתִּי teaches 'even on שבת,' meaning the man may carry a sick goat. If carrying were already forbidden on every יום הכיפורים, a special teaching for שבת would add nothing, because the goat is always sent on יום הכיפורים. So רפרם concludes that on a regular יום הכיפורים there is no הוצאה problem. The problem only exists when it is also שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This means.' Signals an inference drawn from what was just said.
עירוב חצרות, the arrangement that allows carrying between shared domains
Carrying an object from one domain to another
An אמורא who makes the inference here

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one extra word in a פסוק can reveal a broad rule about the laws of יום הכיפורים.

phrases.english: Rafram said: This is to say:
eiruv and carrying out apply to Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The extra teaching about Shabbat was needed only because of these rules.

phrases.english: but eiruv and carrying out do not apply to Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב ששת's explanation (now accepted by everyone) to infer a general rule about יום הכיפורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prohibitions of עירוב and הוצאה apply to שבת but not to יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: What does 'even in impurity' come to teach?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא said עִתִּי means 'even בטומאה'. The גמרא asks what practical law that teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'appointed' teaches that he may send the goat even in a state of impurity. For what law is this needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the next part of the ברייתא's teaching on עִתִּי and asks what it means in practice. This step sets up רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the goat is sent 'even בטומאה' but did not say whose impurity, or what is being allowed. The גמרא wants a concrete case where this teaching changes the law.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Appointed' or 'ready.' The word in the פסוק describing the man who sends the goat
Ritual impurity
'For what law?' Asks for the practical result of a teaching

phrases.english: "Appointed": even in impurity.
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא.

phrases.english: For what law is this needed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'even on שבת' teaching to the 'even בטומאה' teaching of the same word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical case the teaching 'even בטומאה' is about.

steps.title: An impure sender may enter the courtyard and send the goat
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that if the man sending the goat becomes impure, he may still enter the עזרה while impure and send it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It teaches that if the sender became impure, he enters the עזרה while impure and sends the goat away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question: the 'impurity' refers to the man who sends the goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an impure person may not enter the עזרה. Here the teaching makes an exception for the appointed man. Even if he became impure, he may enter to take the goat and send it.

keyTerms.meaning: Became impure
The Temple courtyard
The one who sends it (the goat's escort)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It is to say that if the one sending it became impure,
he enters the courtyard while impure and sends it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לוֹמַר שֶׁאִם נִטְמָא מְשַׁלְּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An impure sender may enter the עזרה and send the goat.

steps.title: If the goat gets sick: רבי אליעזר sidesteps
steps.stepSummary: Students ask רבי אליעזר whether a sick goat may be carried on the shoulder. He answers that the goat is strong enough to carry both him and them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי אליעזר: If the goat became sick, may he carry it on his shoulder? He said to them: It can carry me and you!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related story. Students ask רבי אליעזר a practical question, and he avoids giving a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same case רב ששת dealt with: carrying a sick goat. רבי אליעזר does not say yes or no. He only says that a healthy goat chosen for this job will not get sick.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They asked רבי אליעזר.' Opens a series of questions to him
Became sick
Carry it on his shoulder

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is not saying 'no.' He avoids the question completely, so his answers are not rulings.

phrases.english: They asked Rabbi Eliezer:
If it became sick, may he carry it on his shoulder?
He said to them:
It is able to carry me and you.
phrases.notes: Meaning: the goat is strong and will not get sick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected by topic to רב ששת's case of the sick goat.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a sick goat be carried on the escort's shoulder?

steps.title: If the sender gets sick: רבי אליעזר sidesteps again
steps.stepSummary: They ask whether a sick sender may hand the goat to someone else. רבי אליעזר answers, 'May I and you be well.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If the sender became sick, may he send the goat through someone else? He said to them: May I and you be well!
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask a second practical question, and רבי אליעזר again avoids ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the problem is the man, not the goat. רבי אליעזר answers with a wish for good health. This suggests the case will not happen, so he gives no actual law.

keyTerms.meaning: Through another person
'May I be well.' A polite way of avoiding the question

phrases.english: If the one sending it became sick,
may he send it through someone else?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: אֱהֵא בְּשָׁלוֹם אֲנִי וְאַתֶּם.
phrases.english: He said to them: May I and you be well.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָלָה מְשַׁלְּחוֹ, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּשַׁלְּחֶנּוּ בְּיַד אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second question in the same series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a sick sender hand the goat to another person?

steps.title: If the goat survives the fall: רבי אליעזר sidesteps a third time
steps.stepSummary: They ask whether, if the goat survives being pushed off the cliff, he should go down and kill it. רבי אליעזר quotes a פסוק: 'So may all Your enemies perish, ה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he pushed it and it did not die, should he go down after it and kill it? He said to them: 'So may all Your enemies perish, O Lord.'
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask a third question, and רבי אליעזר again answers with a phrase instead of a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק from שירת דבורה suggests that the goat will surely die, just as the enemies of ה׳ are destroyed. So he does not rule whether to go down and kill it.

keyTerms.meaning: He pushed it (off the cliff)
And kill it
'So may all Your enemies perish' (שופטים ה:לא)

phrases.english: If he pushed it and it did not die,
should he go down after it and kill it?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: ״כֵּן יֹאבְדוּ כׇל אוֹיְבֶיךָ ה׳״.
phrases.english: He said to them: "So may all Your enemies perish, O Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּחָפוֹ וְלֹא מֵת, מַהוּ שֶׁיֵּרֵד אַחֲרָיו וִימִיתֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third question in the same series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If the goat survives the fall, must he go down and kill it?

steps.title: The חכמים answer all three questions directly
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים rule: a sick goat is carried on the shoulder, a sick sender passes the goat to someone else, and a goat that survives the fall is killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: If it became sick, he carries it on his shoulder. If the sender became sick, he sends it through someone else. If he pushed it and it did not die, he goes down after it and kills it.
steps.whatsHappening: In contrast to רבי אליעזר, the חכמים give a clear 'yes' to all three questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ruling matches one of the three questions, in the same order. Carrying the sick goat also fits רב ששת's earlier explanation of 'even on שבת'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the Sages say.' Introduces the majority view
He carries it (on his shoulder)
He goes down after it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר avoided all three questions. The חכמים allow all three: carrying a sick goat, replacing a sick sender, and killing a goat that survived the fall.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
If it became sick, he carries it on his shoulder;
if the one sending it became sick, he sends it through someone else.

phrases.aramaic: דְּחָפוֹ וְלֹא מֵת — יֵרֵד אַחֲרָיו וִימִיתֶנּוּ.
phrases.english: If he pushed it and it did not die, he goes down after it and kills it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives clear rulings on the three questions רבי אליעזר avoided.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick goat is carried, a sick sender is replaced, and a goat that survives the fall is killed.

steps.title: Asking about a certain man's share in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי אליעזר whether a certain man has a portion in עולם הבא. He deflects with a counter-remark.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי אליעזר: What about פלוני, does he have a place in עולם הבא? He told them: Is פלוני the only one you are asking me about?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask about the fate of a specific (apparently wicked) person, and רבי אליעזר does not give a direct answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the pattern from Steps 11–13: a question comes, and רבי אליעזר sidesteps it. His reply, 'You only asked about So-and-so?', turns the question around instead of ruling. The גמרא will explain this pattern in Step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: So-and-so; an unnamed person
The World-to-Come
'You have only asked me about…' (his deflecting formula)

phrases.english: They asked Rabbi Eliezer:
So-and-so, what is he regarding the World-to-Come?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם לֹא שְׁאֶלְתּוּנִי אֶלָּא עַל פְּלוֹנִי.
phrases.english: He said to them: You have only asked me about So-and-so?
phrases.notes: He's dodging the question here, not answering it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of questions put to רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a certain person has a portion in עולם הבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No direct answer; he deflects with a counter-remark.

steps.title: Saving a ewe from a lion
steps.stepSummary: They ask whether a shepherd may rescue a ewe from a lion (on שבת, per the מאירי). He deflects again.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law about a shepherd saving a ewe from a lion? He told them: Is the ewe the only thing you are asking me about?
steps.whatsHappening: Another practical question, and רבי אליעזר again avoids giving a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the מאירי, the question is about rescuing an animal on שבת. Instead of ruling, רבי אליעזר shifts attention to the ewe itself. The pattern of not answering continues.

keyTerms.meaning: To rescue
A ewe (female sheep)
Lion

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ לְהַצִּיל רוֹעֶה כִּבְשָׂה מִן הָאֲרִי?
phrases.english: What is the law about a shepherd saving a ewe from the lion?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: לֹא שְׁאֶלְתּוּנִי אֶלָּא עַל הַכִּבְשָׂה.
phrases.english: He said to them: You have only asked me about the ewe?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ לְהַצִּיל רוֹעֶה כִּבְשָׂה מִן הָאֲרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next question in the same series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a shepherd may save the ewe from a lion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Deflection: 'You only asked about the ewe?'

steps.title: Saving the shepherd from a lion
steps.stepSummary: They switch to asking about saving the shepherd himself. He deflects in the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law about saving the shepherd from the lion? He told them: Is the shepherd the only one you are asking me about?
steps.whatsHappening: The students try the question from another angle, now about the person instead of the animal. He still does not answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the case from animal to human does not get a ruling out of him either. His reply copies the exact wording of the last one, which shows this is a deliberate pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: Shepherd

phrases.english: What is the law about saving the shepherd from the lion?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: לֹא שְׁאֶלְתּוּנִי אֶלָּא עַל הָרוֹעֶה.
phrases.english: He said to them: You have only asked me about the shepherd?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A variation on the previous question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may save the shepherd from the lion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Deflection: 'You only asked about the shepherd?'

steps.title: Does a ממזר inherit?
steps.stepSummary: They ask whether a ממזר inherits from his parents. He answers with a question: what about whether he does יבום?
steps.simpleTranslation: A ממזר: does he inherit? (He answered:) And what about whether he does יבום?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask a question about a ממזר's inheritance, and רבי אליעזר answers with a different question instead of a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier replies, here he does not repeat 'you only asked me…'. He asks a related question of his own, about יבום. Either way, no ruling is given.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden union
To inherit
To perform levirate marriage (יבום)

steps.confusionAlert: The two questions do not both come from the students. The first (inheriting) is theirs; the second (יבום) is רבי אליעזר's counter-question.

phrases.english: A mamzer: what is he regarding inheriting?
phrases.notes: Here the students are asking him.

phrases.english: (He replied:) What about performing levirate marriage?
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר answers with a question of his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same series, with a new style of deflection.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A counter-question about יבום instead of a ruling.

steps.title: Plastering one's house
steps.stepSummary: They ask whether one may plaster his house (after the חורבן). He counters by asking about plastering a grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law about plastering one's house? (He answered:) What about plastering one's grave?
steps.whatsHappening: Another question meets another counter-question. This is the last item in the list before the גמרא explains his behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about plastering a home after the destruction of the בית המקדש. He replies by asking about a grave, which again avoids giving a ruling. This sets up the גמרא's explanation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To plaster (with lime)
Grave

phrases.english: What is the law about plastering one's house?
phrases.notes: Here the students are asking him.

phrases.english: (He replied:) What about plastering one's grave?
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר answers with a question of his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final question in the series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may plaster his house.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A counter-question about plastering a grave.

steps.title: Why רבי אליעזר did not answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that he was not brushing them off. He simply never said anything he had not heard from his רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was not because he was pushing them away with words. Rather, it was because he never in his life said something he had not heard from his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and explains the whole pattern of non-answers from Steps 11–19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think רבי אליעזר was dodging because he did not know the answers, or was being dismissive. The גמרא rejects that. He held strictly to his tradition: on questions where he had no received teaching, he would not invent a ruling, so he deflected instead.

keyTerms.meaning: That he distanced them with words (put them off)
From the mouth of his teacher
Ever, in all his days

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's deflections are not evasion. They signal 'I have no tradition on this from my רבי', and he would never say something he had not received.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains all the strange replies in this sugya, and it shows how strongly רבי אליעזר was committed to received tradition.

phrases.english: Not because he was putting them off with words.
Rather, because he did not say anything
that he had not heard from his teacher's mouth, ever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the pattern of deflections in all the previous questions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: He deflected because he had no tradition from his teacher, not because he lacked knowledge or wanted to dismiss them.

steps.title: A wise woman asks about the deaths after the עגל
steps.stepSummary: A wise woman asks why the sinners of the עגל died in different ways when they all shared in the sin. He deflects her by quoting a פסוק about women spinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: A wise woman asked רבי אליעזר: Since everyone was equally involved in the sin of the עגל, why did they not all die the same way? He told her: A woman's wisdom is only in the spindle, as the פסוק says: 'And every wise-hearted woman spun with her hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new question comes to רבי אליעזר, this time from a woman, about the sin of the עגל. He does not answer her directly either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her question points to a real difficulty: some died by the sword, some by plague, and some by an intestinal illness. He does not answer it. Instead he dismisses her with a פסוק about women's skill in spinning, implying she should not concern herself with such questions. The גמרא then supplies the answer itself through the dispute of רב and לוי in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A wise woman
The sin of the Golden Calf
Their deaths
Spindle (used for spinning thread)
They spun

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלָה אִשָּׁה חֲכָמָה אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: A wise woman asked Rabbi Eliezer:
Since they were equal in the deed of the Calf,
why were their deaths not equal?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהּ: אֵין חׇכְמָה לָאִשָּׁה אֶלָּא בְּפֶלֶךְ,
phrases.english: He said to her: A woman has no wisdom except in the spindle,
and so it says:
'And every wise-hearted woman spun with her hands.'
phrases.notes: שמות לה:כה

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלָה אִשָּׁה חֲכָמָה אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new questioner and topic, still showing רבי אליעזר not answering directly.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why those who sinned equally at the עגל died different deaths.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No direct answer; he deflects with a פסוק about women's wisdom in spinning.

steps.title: First view: the punishment matched how a person sinned
steps.stepSummary: One of רב and לוי says the three deaths match three levels of action: real worship, showing affection to the idol, and only being happy inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated that רב and לוי disagreed. One said: whoever sacrificed and burned incense to the calf died by the sword. Whoever hugged and kissed it died by a plague. Whoever was only happy about it in his heart died from a stomach disease called הדרוקן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the question the wise woman asked in step 21: why did the sinners of the עגל die in different ways? This is the first of two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view sorts people by what they actually did. Sacrificing and burning incense are real acts of worship, so they got the sword (death through a human court). Hugging and kissing are less serious acts, so they got a plague from Heaven, and someone who did nothing but feel glad inside got הדרוקן.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
Sacrificed and burned incense (real acts of worship)
Hugged and kissed (signs of love for the idol)
Sword
A swelling disease of the stomach

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav and Levi (disagreed).
phrases.notes: Sets up a disagreement between two אמוראים.

phrases.english: One said:
phrases.notes: We are not told which of the two said this.

phrases.english: Whoever sacrificed and burned incense died by the sword.
phrases.notes: Killed by the Levites, who carried out משה's order.

phrases.english: Whoever hugged and kissed it died by death (a plague).
phrases.notes: Refers to the plague ה׳ sent.

phrases.english: Whoever was glad in his heart died by הדרוקן.
phrases.notes: A stomach illness, connected to the water משה made them drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the answer the woman did not get in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did the sinners of the עגל die in three different ways?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The type of death matched the kind of action: worship meant the sword, affection meant a plague, and inner joy meant הדרוקן.

steps.title: Second view: the punishment depended on witnesses and warning
steps.stepSummary: The other of רב and לוי says the three deaths depended on whether there were witnesses and a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: if there were witnesses and a warning, the person died by the sword. If there were witnesses but no warning, he died by a plague. If there were no witnesses and no warning, he died from הדרוקן.
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion gives a different reason for the three kinds of death. Here the question is not what the person did, but what proof and warning there were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, all of them may have done real worship. A human court can only kill someone if there are witnesses and a התראה, so only those people got the sword. Those with witnesses but no warning were left for Heaven's plague, and those with no witnesses at all died secretly from הדרוקן.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses
A warning given before the sin, needed for a court to punish
Death (here, a plague from Heaven)

steps.confusionAlert: Both views agree on the same three deaths: sword, plague, and הדרוקן. They only argue about who got which one.

phrases.english: And the other one said:
phrases.notes: The second of רב and לוי.

phrases.english: With witnesses and a warning, by the sword,
phrases.notes: Like a regular court case.

phrases.english: With witnesses but no warning, by a plague,
phrases.notes: A court cannot punish without a warning.

phrases.english: With no witnesses and no warning, by הדרוקן.
phrases.notes: A hidden sin, punished in a hidden way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, competing explanation to the one in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did the sinners of the עגל die in three different ways?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It depended on proof: witnesses plus a warning meant the sword, witnesses alone meant a plague, and neither meant הדרוקן.

steps.title: שבט לוי did not worship the עגל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that not one member of שבט לוי served עבודה זרה, and he brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: the tribe of Levi did not serve idols, as it says, "And משה stood at the gate of the camp" (and said, "Whoever is for ה׳, come to me," and all the sons of Levi gathered to him).
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רב יהודה teaches that the whole tribe of Levi stayed away from the עגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the end of the פסוק, which is not quoted but is meant by וגו׳: "all the sons of Levi gathered to him." If all of them came to משה's side, then none of them had served the עגל.

keyTerms.meaning: The tribe of Levi
Idol worship
The gate of the camp
"Etc." The rest of the פסוק is meant, even though it is not quoted

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל לֵוִי לֹא עָבַד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: The tribe of Levi did not serve idols,
phrases.notes: This means the whole tribe, every single member.

phrases.english: as it is said:
"And Moshe stood at the gate of the camp, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות לב:כו. The proof is in the end of the פסוק: "all the sons of Levi gathered to him."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: שִׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל לֵוִי לֹא עָבַד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a related topic: who took no part in the sin of the עגל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No member of שבט לוי served the עגל, based on the פסוק saying all the sons of Levi gathered to משה.

steps.title: Challenge: a פסוק suggests that relatives of the לויים were killed
steps.stepSummary: When רבינא repeats רב יהודה's teaching, the sons of רב פפא בר אבא challenge it with the פסוק about Levi saying of his father and mother, "I have not seen him."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא sat and said this teaching. The sons of רב פפא בר אבא challenged רבינא: the פסוק says about Levi, "Who said of his father and his mother, 'I have not seen him.'"
steps.whatsHappening: The first line sets the scene: רבינא was teaching רב יהודה's statement. Then the sons of רב פפא בר אבא attack it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק praises the Levites for killing the sinners without sparing even close family members. If a Levite's own father or brother was among those killed, then some members of שבט לוי did serve the עגל. That contradicts רב יהודה's claim that the whole tribe stayed clean.

keyTerms.meaning: He sat and was saying (teaching)
A teaching or statement
They challenged him (usually from a written source)
"I have not seen him" (I did not let family ties stop me)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא's answer to this challenge has not come yet. Do not assume רב יהודה has been proven wrong; the next step will respond.

phrases.english: Ravina sat and said this teaching.
phrases.notes: The teaching he's saying is רב יהודה's, the one about שבט לוי.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ בְּנֵי רַב פָּפָּא בַּר אַבָּא לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: The sons of Rav Pappa bar Abba challenged Ravina:
"Who said of his father and of his mother: I have not seen him."
phrases.notes: דברים לג:ט. This suggests the Levites killed their own relatives, so those relatives were Levites who had sinned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ בְּנֵי רַב פָּפָּא בַּר אַבָּא לְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב יהודה's statement in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that no member of שבט לוי served עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק praises Levites for killing even a father or brother. A Levite's father or brother is also a Levite, so some Levites must have sinned.

steps.title: The relatives in the פסוק were ישראלים from the mother's side
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that 'his father, brothers, sons' in the פסוק mean relatives through the mother, who were from ישראל, not from שבט לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: "His father" means his mother's father, who was a ישראל. "His brothers" means his half-brothers from his mother, whose father was a ישראל. "His sons" means his daughter's sons, whose father was a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge from step 25. The relatives that the לויים had to kill were not from שבט לוי at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tribe follows the father. So a mother's father, half-brothers from the mother, and a daughter's sons can all be ישראלים even though they are relatives of a לוי. The פסוק therefore does not prove that any לוי worshipped the עגל, and רב יהודה's teaching stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: his mother's father (maternal grandfather)
his brothers from his mother (maternal half-brothers)
his daughter's sons
from a regular Israelite (not from שבט לוי)

steps.whatToRemember: Tribe goes by the father. So a לוי can have close relatives who are ישראלים. That is how the פסוק fits with the claim that no לוי served the עגל.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק does not mean the לוי's own father or full brothers. Each word is read as a relative through a woman, so that relative belongs to a different tribe.

phrases.english: "His father" means his mother's father, an Israelite;
"his brothers" means his brothers from his mother, fathered by an Israelite;
"his sons" means his daughter's sons from an Israelite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of the sons of רב פפא בר אבא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק: the relatives are maternal relatives from a different tribe
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to say that לויים killed their own fathers, brothers and sons, so some לויים must have sinned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The relatives were ישראלים related through women. No member of שבט לוי served the עגל.

steps.title: The 'Babylonians' were really Alexandrians
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה about the ramp, רבה בר בר חנה says the rude people were Alexandrians. They were called Babylonians only because people disliked Babylonians.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'They made a ramp for it', etc. רבה בר בר חנה said: They were not Babylonians, they were Alexandrians. Because people hated the Babylonians, they called these rude people by the Babylonians' name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה, which said a ramp was built because 'Babylonians' would pull the goat's hair. רבה בר בר חנה explains who these people really were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה blamed 'Babylonians' for the bad behavior. רבה בר בר חנה says the real troublemakers were Jews from Alexandria in Egypt. 'Babylonian' was used as an insulting label for any foreigners who acted badly.

keyTerms.meaning: a ramp or raised walkway
Babylonians
Alexandrians (Jews from Alexandria, Egypt)
they called them by their (the Babylonians') name

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] And they made a ramp for it, etc.
Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
They were not Babylonians,
rather, they were Alexandrians.
And since they hate the Babylonians,
they would call them by their name.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֶבֶשׁ עָשׂוּ לוֹ כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עגל discussion and returns to explaining the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'Babylonians' in the משנה were really Alexandrians. The name was used as an insult.

steps.title: A ברייתא from רבי יהודה says the same, and רבי יוסי is relieved
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי יהודה saying they were Alexandrians, not Babylonians. רבי יוסי thanks him for putting his mind at ease.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says, they were not Babylonians, they were Alexandrians. רבי יוסי said to him: May your mind be at ease, because you have put my mind at ease.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבה בר בר חנה. רבי יוסי, whose family came from Babylonia, is happy to hear it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says exactly what רבה בר בר חנה said, so his claim is backed by a תנא. רבי יוסי's warm blessing shows how much it bothered Babylonian Jews to be blamed for the rude behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
may your mind be at ease (a blessing of thanks)
since you have put my mind at ease

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
They were not Babylonians,
rather, they were Alexandrians.
Rabbi Yosei said to him:
May your mind be at ease,
since you have put my mind at ease.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה בר בר חנה with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבה בר בר חנה's claim that the troublemakers were Alexandrians

steps.title: What 'take and go' really meant
steps.stepSummary: A תוספתא gives the full saying: why is this goat lingering while the generation's sins are so many?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said they would say: 'Take and go.' It was taught: they meant, 'Why is this goat waiting here, when the sins of the generation are so many?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the shout quoted in the משנה, 'take and go', by bringing the longer wording from a תוספתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Take and go' sounds rude by itself. The תוספתא shows that the people were urging the goat to hurry and carry away their many sins. It was an impatient cry for כפרה, not just a random insult.

keyTerms.meaning: take [our sins] and go
the goat (Aramaic)
linger, delay
the sins of the generation are many

phrases.english: [The משנה said they would say:] Take and go.
It was taught: Why does this goat linger,
when the sins of the generation are many?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same part of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Take and go' was a plea for the goat to hurry and carry off the many sins of the generation.

steps.title: Important people escort the goat-leader, with ten booths on the way
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: prominent people of ירושלים walked with the goat-leader to the first booth. There were ten booths from ירושלים to the cliff.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Some of the important people of ירושלים would walk with him as far as the first booth. There were ten booths from ירושלים to the cliff,
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes the trip of the man leading the שעיר המשתלח out to the wilderness. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man leading the goat was not sent off alone. Respected people walked with him, and rest booths were set up along the route. This prepares the details about the booths that come next.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (start of a new משנה)
the prominent, honored people of ירושלים
escort, accompany
booth, a resting hut along the route
the cliff in the wilderness

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Some of the prominent people of Jerusalem would escort him
until the first booth.
There were ten booths from Jerusalem to the cliff,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִיַּקִּירֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם הָיוּ מְלַוִּין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after finishing the explanation of the previous one
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The goat-leader was escorted by prominent people to the first of ten booths set up between ירושלים and the cliff.
